headline: Machine learning on public transcriptomes nominates candidate biomarkers across diseases
label: Integrative Biomarker Discovery Pipelines
summary: Many disease studies now pair public transcriptomes with ML feature selection, while inferential strength varies widely across designs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is candidate-gene prioritization, in which screening of public transcriptomic data is paired with machine learning and downstream checks to nominate biomarkers or hub genes. Many items combine differential expression, WGCNA or multiple ML algorithms, as in the six-gene OSA panel (AUC 0.72-0.78) and the three-gene NEC signature. Several add single-cell RNA-seq, as in HMGN2 in heart failure, while others add RT-qPCR validation, as in keloid CCL20 and NLRC4. What is new is the extension beyond expression levels: RNA modification gene sets (m6A/m7G/m5C/m1A in ulcerative colitis, ac4C in osteoarthritis), alternative splicing and RBP regulators in liver transplantation injury, and a Ridge regression study predicting protein abundance from transcriptomes across 940 cancer cell lines. Inferential strength varies considerably across these designs, and not all items include experimental validation.
